run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-15T08:26:11Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend RequestErrorRate alert is explained by a failing dependency: the single-replica ad service pod ad-554b849958-l9ft5 in namespace otel-demo is being repeatedly OOM-killed and is stuck in CrashLoopBackOff, so frontend's gRPC calls to oteldemo.AdService/GetAds fail at connect time and the /api/data route that depends on them returns errors. Frontend's own error spans are exclusively on that path (GET, GET /api/data, executing api route (pages) /api/data, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, plus tcp.connect failures), and the frontend→AdService error counter starts rising between 08:25:00 and 08:26:00, matching the first kubelet BackOff event at 08:25:25, while the successful AdService client-span counter freezes. ad's own GetAds server spans carry no error status, so the failure is at the connection level while the container is down/restarting, not an application error inside ad. frontend-proxy records matching ingress/egress error spans. Span-based frontend error ratio was 1.19% at 08:26:11 and 7.27% at 08:36:00 (span-based, not a request error rate). Residual unknowns: the alert's own rule/denominator was not found, span metrics stop advancing at 08:35:00, and cAdvisor's sampled memory maxima for the ad containers (372.6 MB) sit below the deployment's 450Mi limit, so the exact OOM mechanism is unresolved even though the OOMKilled terminations are direct evidence.

claims.text: frontend emitted STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans inside 07:26:11-08:43:44 confined to one dependency path: 552 on span_name GET, 552 on GET /api/data, 552 on 'executing api route (pages) /api/data', 552 on grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, and 19.28 on tcp.connect; all other frontend operations (GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, CartService, CheckoutService, ProductCatalogService, RecommendationService) had 0 error spans.

The frontend client-span counter for grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR was flat at 367 from 08:10:00 through 08:25:00, then rose 400 (08:26), 456 (08:27), 519 (08:28), 567 (08:29), 626 (08:30), 687 (08:31), 741 (08:32), 810 (08:33), 869 (08:34), 911 (08:35); the paired STATUS_CODE_UNSET counter last increased at 08:26:00 (1578 -> 1600) and stayed at 1600 afterwards.

AdService/GetAds error activity begins between 08:25:00 and 08:26:00; a separate 600s-step view of frontend error spans shows 0 before the 08:16:11 evaluation point, 34.74 in the window ending 08:26:11, and 475.27 in the window ending 08:36:11 for GET, GET /api/data, 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, with tcp.connect showing 9.47 and 8.36 in those two windows.

Pod ad-554b849958-l9ft5 (namespace otel-demo) has container 'ad' with restartCount 4, lastState.terminated exitCode 137 reason OOMKilled (started 08:26:55, finished 08:27:25) and current state.terminated exitCode 137 reason OOMKilled (started 08:28:16, finished 08:28:27); the pod's Ready and ContainersReady conditions are False with reason ContainersNotReady since 08:28:28.

Kubernetes events for pod ad-554b849958-l9ft5 include Warning reason BackOff on spec.containers{ad}, count 23, firstTimestamp 08:25:25 and lastTimestamp 08:33:04, alongside Normal Pulled/Created/Started events for the same container.

Deployment 'ad' in otel-demo runs replicas: 1 with container ad image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad and resources limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi, requests cpu 10m / memory 225Mi; pod listing shows exactly one ad pod, so a single OOM-killed container removes all ad endpoints.

ad container memory working set for the pod-level cgroup was 333,307,904 B at 08:01:11, 348,856,320 B at 08:06:11, 362,237,952 B at 08:11:11 and 371,359,744 B at 08:16:11, then dropped to 53,465,088 B at 08:26:11, 151,400,448 B at 08:31:11 and 245,760 B at 08:36:11, consistent with container restarts.

At 30s resolution the ad container working set of the first container instance (id cri-containerd-0660c518...) stayed flat at 370,941,952-371,867,648 B from 08:20:11 to 08:29:11, while new container ids appear at 08:26:11 (c201950..., 51,388,416 -> 66,813,952 B), 08:27:11 (d11f8bd..., 2,281,472 -> 59,408,384 -> 183,771,136 B) and 08:30:11 (4d341002..., 41,209,856 -> 58,597,376 -> 123,588,608 B).

The ad service's own spans show no errors on oteldemo.AdService/GetAds: 1348.54 STATUS_CODE_UNSET and 0 error in the window, with getAdsByCategory 1167.93 and getRandomAds 377.47 UNSET; the only ad error spans are 2.03 on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream.
Whole-window STATUS_CODE_ERROR span increases by service were: frontend 2227.28, frontend-proxy 1122.26, ad 2.03, fraud-detection 3.05, recommendation 3.04, accounting 0, payment 0.
frontend-proxy error spans in the window are only on span_name 'ingress' (569.25) and 'router frontend egress' (553.01), i.e. on its traffic to the frontend component.

Span-based frontend error ratio (sum(rate(error spans[5m]))/sum(rate(all frontend spans[5m]))) was 0.01191 at 2026-11-15T08:26:11Z and 0.07268 at 2026-11-15T08:36:00Z; this is a span ratio, not the alert's request error rate.

The remaining error spans outside the frontend dependency path are all on flagd event streams: ad 2.03 and fraud-detection 3.05 on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream and recommendation 3.04 on /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream, with ResolveBoolean/ResolveInt variants at 0.

Node i-0d81a0f472ebdc704, which hosts pod ad-554b849958-l9ft5, reports MemoryPressure False, DiskPressure False, PIDPressure False and Ready True at the time of the query, and the pod list shows all other otel-demo pods with restartCount 0 except ad (4 restarts).

All frontend span-metric counters stop advancing after 08:35:00 (STATUS_CODE_ERROR frozen at 4135, STATUS_CODE_UNSET frozen at 131955) even though series samples continue to 08:39:00, so span evidence does not describe the frontend state after about 08:35.
The frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-jfvbx is Running with restartCount 0 and owner ReplicaSet frontend-675fd7b5c5, i.e. the frontend process itself was not restarted during the window.

Primary explanation: container 'ad' in pod ad-554b849958-l9ft5 exceeds its memory limit and is OOM-killed repeatedly (exit 137, reason OOMKilled, restartCount 4, 23 BackOff events from 08:25:25). Because the ad deployment has only one replica, no ready ad endpoint remains, so frontend's gRPC GetAds calls fail at connection level (tcp.connect error spans, client spans STATUS_CODE_ERROR starting 08:25-08:26 while UNSET successes stop), the /api/data route and its HTTP spans return errors, the error rate the alert watches rises above 0, and frontend-proxy records matching ingress and frontend-egress error spans.

Unresolved sub-question of the same cause: the ad container memory growth is fast (fresh instances reached 123.6 MB and 183.8 MB within 1-2 minutes of start, and the initial instance climbed 333.3 MB -> 371.4 MB over 15 minutes before the first OOM), which could be either an under-provisioned 450Mi limit for normal ad workload or a memory growth pattern that saturates the limit between scrapes; the evidence distinguishes neither, and no change history is available for the ad workload.

cAdvisor's sampled maxima for the ad containers do not themselves show the 450Mi limit being reached: container_memory_max_usage_bytes maxima were 372,563,968 B (0660c518...), 189,325,312 B (3b56c468...), 123,789,312 B (4d341002...), 49,790,976 B (a72e9cb...) and container_memory_usage_bytes maxima were 372,006,912 B, 189,317,120 B, 123,707,392 B, 183,910,400 B, all below 450Mi = 471,859,200 B; a pod-level working-set maximum of 471,658,496 B was observed but the pod-level series also sums overlapping container cgroups, so it does not by itself prove a per-container limit hit.

The ad application layer stayed healthy in its own telemetry: oteldemo.AdService/GetAds server spans show 1348.54 UNSET and 0 errors, and ad continued writing normal request log lines ('Targeted ad request received for [...]', 'Non-targeted ad request received, preparing random response.') at 08:23-08:24 while it was still running; this supports a connection-level failure rather than ad application errors.

The small flagd error spans (ad 2.03, fraud-detection 3.05, recommendation 3.04, all on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream) are considered and rejected as the cause of the frontend alert: they are on a different operation, quantities are 2-3 spans over 77 minutes, and frontend's 2227.28 error spans occur only on the AdService/GetAds and /api/data path plus tcp.connect.

A node-level memory problem and a frontend restart are rejected as explanations: node i-0d81a0f472ebdc704 reports MemoryPressure False and Ready True, every otel-demo pod except ad has restartCount 0, and frontend-675fd7b5c5-jfvbx is Running with 0 restarts, so the failures originate from the ad container's own OOM terminations.

Raise the ad container memory limit or right-size the ad workload (current limit 450Mi, request 225Mi) and profile ad's memory growth after start; then confirm with `kubectl logs --previous` on ad-554b849958-l9ft5 and with container memory alerts, since the current tool run could not read the previous container's logs.
Give the ad service more than one replica (currently replicas: 1) so that a single OOM-killed container does not leave the service with no ready endpoint and turn into frontend /api/data errors.

gaps: The alert's own rule could not be verified: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name RequestErrorRate returned no_data, so the metric and denominator behind the reported value 2.622222222222222 are unknown and were not reproduced.

No kube-state-metrics series were available in this Prometheus: get_metric_names for {__name__=~"kube_.*"} returned nothing and kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="otel-demo"} returned no series, so deployment/ReplicaSet/availability time series for ad and frontend are unknown.

frontend container logs for 08:10-08:43 returned no lines at all (with and without an error filter), so the frontend-side gRPC error text (e.g. connection refused vs deadline exceeded) could not be read.

ad container logs read only to 08:24:16 and the previous container instance was unavailable (HTTP 400 'previous terminated container "ad" not found'), so ad's output at the moment of each OOM kill is unknown.

Span-derived metrics stop advancing at 08:35:00 for frontend (and the AdService error counter stops at 08:35:00 while samples continue to 08:39:00), so whether the error rate and the alert persisted after ~08:35 is unknown; no recovery can be claimed.

The exact mechanism of the OOM is unresolved: cAdvisor maxima for the ad containers (up to 372,563,968 B) are below the deployment's 450Mi limit (471,859,200 B), and it cannot be determined from the available samples whether an allocation spike between scrapes, a different effective limit, or another memory consumer inside the cgroup triggered the kill.

Trace evidence is a biased Jaeger sample: tag searches for error=true, otel.status_code="ERROR", rpc.grpc.status_code="14" and http.status_code="500" on frontend and frontend-proxy returned no traces, so per-span error messages and HTTP status codes for the failing requests could not be read.

The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so no deployment or configuration change timeline (e.g. whether ad's memory limit was recently lowered, or the 2.1.3-ad image recently rolled out) is available; the ad pod's start time 07:47:47Z is shared by all otel-demo pods, which is consistent with an environment start rather than an ad-specific rollout, but this is not proven.
next_steps: Read the ad container's previous-instance logs (kubectl logs --previous ad-554b849958-l9ft5 -c ad -n otel-demo) around 08:25-08:29 to see the process output immediately before each OOM kill.
Retrieve the RequestErrorRate alerting rule definition from the Alertmanager/Prometheus configuration to confirm which metric and denominator produce the reported 2.622 value.
Check whether ad's effective memory limit matches the deployment's 450Mi (LimitRange, VPA or admission mutation) and collect higher-resolution ad memory samples around 08:25-08:29.
Confirm current state of pod ad-554b849958-l9ft5 and the RequestErrorRate alert after 08:43, since span metrics stopped advancing at 08:35 in this data set.
If ad memory growth reproduces, capture a heap/allocation profile of the ad service under the load-generator workload before adjusting the limit.
